title: Athanasius against the world
hook: exiled again and again, he held to Nicaea when it was unpopular

segments.voice: Yesterday, homoousios: of one substance, the Son is what the Father is. Your line: true god from true god.

Winning the vote isn't the end of an argument. Nicaea chose its word, and the argument kept going. Bishops who'd signed changed their minds. Emperors came and went, and some leaned toward Arius' side. And one stubborn bishop of Alexandria, Athanasius, would not let the word go. He was sent away from his city and came back, sent away again and came back again. He hid. He wrote. He was accused of crimes, and answered the charges in writing. Later generations gave him a short Latin nickname: Athanasius contra mundum. Athanasius against the world. It didn't look like a hero on a hill. It looked like a man packing a bag, again.

What was he holding on to? In his book On the Incarnation, he gives the reason in one swing of a sentence. In paraphrase: God became human, so that humans might become divine. Only God can bring people home to God, he argued. If the Son is a creature, however grand, the bridge doesn't reach. So homoousios wasn't a word game. It was the whole rescue. Now the exiles. He's sent as far as Trier, in Gaul, a long way from the Nile. Other times he disappears into Egypt, sheltered, the stories say, by the desert monks. He later wrote the Life of Antony, the man who heard a Gospel line read in church and went into the desert. Here's a surprise. When enemies mocked him for running instead of staying to die, he wrote a defense of his flight. Jesus himself withdrew when they sought to kill him, he pointed out. And Paul escaped Damascus this way: "through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands." Standing firm, for Athanasius, didn't mean standing still for the soldiers. It meant not changing the word. Run if you must, hide if you must, but don't sign what you believe is false. Was he easy to deal with? His opponents brought real charges against him, which he denied, and he could be a hard man to cross. But the nickname stuck because, for long stretches, he seemed nearly alone, and he didn't move.
screen: `GOD BECAME HUMAN, SO HUMANS MIGHT RISE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you hold true that isn't popular in some room you're in, at work, at a family table, with friends; it needn't be about faith. Test it slowly: is this a truth, or my pride wearing a truth's clothes? If it holds, look for a way to hold it that isn't cruel to the people who disagree, and if you pray, bring it to God.
Athanasius. The bishop of Alexandria who, exiled again and again, kept holding to the word of Nicaea when it was unpopular.
Your line: against the world. He didn't have to win every room. Seven hundred sixty-nine days.

howItsDone: Orthodox, Catholic and other churches honor Athanasius as a saint and teacher of the faith, and his On the Incarnation is still read in churches and classrooms.
